title: Technical support wait time under memoryless property
scenario_markdown: Caller wait time on hold for enterprise technical support follows an exponential distribution with an average wait time of $\mu = 6$ minutes (rate $\lambda = 1/6\text{ min}^{-1}$). A caller has already waited 5 minutes on hold. Management needs to evaluate the conditional probability that the caller must wait more than 3 additional minutes (total wait time exceeding 8 minutes).
assumptions: Continuous exponential wait time X ~ Exp(lambda = 1/6)
Memoryless property P(X > s + t | X > s) = P(X > t) holds

approval.notes: Verified mathematically: P(X > 8 | X > 5) = P(X > 3) = exp(-3/6) = exp(-0.5) = 0.60653066... Memoryless property algebraically simplifies exp(-8/6)/exp(-5/6) = exp(-0.5). Excel formula: =1 - EXPON.DIST(3, 1/6, TRUE) or =EXP(-0.5).

stages.prompt_markdown: By the memoryless property of the exponential distribution, how does the caller's conditional probability of waiting at least 3 *additional* minutes given that they have already waited 5 minutes, $P(X > 5 + 3 \mid X > 5)$, relate to the unconditional probability $P(X > 3)$?

options.text_markdown: $P(X > 5 + 3 \mid X > 5) = P(X > 3) = e^{-\lambda(3)}$ because the process 'forgets' elapsed wait time
The conditional probability must be much lower than $P(X > 3)$ because the caller has 'put in their time' and service is overdue
options.hint_markdown: The exponential distribution has a constant hazard rate; having waited 5 minutes neither hastens nor delays the arrival of service.

options.text_markdown: The conditional probability must be higher than $P(X > 3)$ because queue congestion compounds as callers wait longer
options.hint_markdown: The exponential distribution models memoryless intervals where the remaining wait time distribution is identical to the original start distribution.

stages.explanation_markdown: The exponential distribution is uniquely memoryless: $P(X > s + t \mid X > s) = \frac{P(X > s + t)}{P(X > s)} = \frac{e^{-\lambda(s+t)}}{e^{-\lambda s}} = e^{-\lambda t} = P(X > t)$. The system forgets elapsed wait time $s = 5$.

stages.prompt_markdown: Calculate this conditional probability: $P(X > 8 \mid X > 5) = P(X > 3) = e^{-3/6} = e^{-0.5}$. Enter as a decimal rounded to at least three places (e.g., 0.607 or 0.6065).
What is the critical managerial implication of the memoryless property for service desk queue management?

options.text_markdown: Elapsed waiting time provides zero predictive power regarding remaining wait time: an agent estimating how long a customer will wait cannot use past wait time as an indicator
First-In-First-Out (FIFO) queue discipline guarantees that memoryless wait times always decrease steadily to zero as customers wait
options.hint_markdown: Queue discipline dictates order of service, but if service completion times are exponential, the remaining duration until completion remains exponential regardless of time elapsed.

options.text_markdown: The probability is computed by simple difference $P(X > 8) - P(X > 5) = e^{-8/6} - e^{-5/6}$
options.hint_markdown: Conditional probability requires dividing by the conditioning event $P(A \cap B)/P(B)$, which simplifies algebraically to $e^{-3/6}$, not a difference.

stages.explanation_markdown: Under memoryless service processes, a customer who has already waited 5 minutes still faces the exact same remaining wait time distribution as a customer who just joined the queue. Past waiting time does not 'earn' faster completion.
